P1.evidence: Best open in the batch on the setter read-back — specific and used to launch the call: 'Kim told me you want to get the fittest you've ever been.' The prospect responded 'Yes, sir' and it framed the whole conversation. The frame itself was two-part and delivered late, after discovery had already started: 'I just really get a good idea where you're at, where you want to go, all that sort of stuff. And then if there's alignment, we'll talk about the coaching. If not, that's fine as well.' No 'what's in the way', no 'what you need', and no agreement was requested. Open question ran: 'What are you looking to achieve?'

P2.evidence: The training and diet half ran well. Training week: 'What kind of training are you doing right now? Are you doing kettlebell stuff or not?' and 'how long have you been doing that for?'. Results were properly explored, including a good calibration question: 'the fittest you've ever been, peak Danny is like a 10 out of 10. Where would you kind of put yourself now in comparison?'. Diet: 'what are you kind of eating right now?' produced a full day's intake. The health half did not run at all. Age 46 was volunteered, not asked. Height, weight, occupation, health conditions and injuries were never raised. Sleep came up only because the prospect raised it himself — 'I have a hard time sleeping because I lifted too much' — and the rep acknowledged it ('that sucks, dude') without asking a single question about it, then later used it back in the pitch as if it had been discovered.

P3.evidence: One genuinely strong move and then nothing. The aesthetics question was excellent and got a vivid answer: 'The 10 out of 10, what does it actually look like? Who is that guy? What does he do? What's different? Let's build it out.' — 'Like an athletic superhero physique kind of guy'. Function was touched only as the prospect's own addendum about moving well and not wrecking his joints. Then the phase stopped. No bridge to what is actually driving it, no 'when you're moving better, what does that do for you', no 'who else does that impact', and no drive-through — despite the prospect naming his kids four separate times, including soccer, basketball and weekend games. He supplied the family thread himself at the very end ('be able to move and stuff and hang out with my kids') and it was never developed. No reflect-back.

P4.evidence: The phase was run only against kettlebells, not against his history: 'Have you ever used kettlebells before, is it brand new?' and 'What held you back from giving it a go, do you think?', which got the honest answer 'I don't know, not doing it right, I guess.' That is a usable root cause and it was dropped in one line. Nothing was asked about what he has tried, what happened, or why anything did or did not stick, and the 'the information isn't the problem' move never came. This prospect is an unusual case — his past attempt largely worked — but that makes the structural argument harder to make, not less necessary, and it was not attempted.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame at all. Nothing about the next two years, no test of willingness to settle at 6 or 7 out of 10, no 'why not', no line in the sand. The prospect had already handed over the exact material for it — 46, recovery getting harder, joints a worry, kids to keep up with — and the rep moved from goals straight to 'if you feel like you're ready, I can walk you through what everything looks like' at the seven-minute mark.

P6.evidence: A process temperature check stood in for the belief question and it worked well: 'How do you feel about it in terms of process, in terms of getting back into kettlebells and getting in the best shape of your life, most importantly?' produced a strong self-summary — 'To me, it sounds really good. It's time efficient. It's going to give me the results.' But it was asked after the presentation, not before, and it was never converted. The all-in question was never asked. That single omission decided the call: 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in on this?' is the exact question that surfaces a spouse before a price is quoted, and instead the wife appeared for the first time after the number, as the reason for the delay.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted so the phase applies. No payment collected. The onboarding call was proposed but never actually booked: 'Book you in your onboarding call with Trevor. We'd do it for Monday' — no confirmation, no calendar invite, no time. No agreement email, no signature on the call, no welcome email, Skool link or questionnaire instruction. The rep then declined the prospect's own same-day close window because of the time difference: 'It's 10 p.m. for me. I will probably be asleep... I'll hit you up tomorrow.'

objection_plays.detail: Textbook trigger at 00:14:58: 'I'm going to talk to my wife... I've to talk to her since it's a large investment.' Zero moves ran. No 'money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you to your goal', no 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain', no 'is this genuinely needing her input or asking permission to bet on yourself', no ownership question, and no deposit-with-refund fallback. The rep's entire response was 'Yeah, it's all good' followed by timezone arithmetic. This is the highest-value single miss in the batch: the prospect had already selected the $9,000 tier and volunteered to confirm within three hours.

No money objection. 'Large investment' was used as the justification for consulting his wife, not as resistance to the price — he moved up a tier on hearing the numbers, from the $6,000 six months to the $9,000 year. Correctly not run.

notes: Sixteen minutes, a warm in-ICP optimizer who upgraded himself to the $9,000 tier unprompted, and the call was lost to a spouse objection that got not one scripted move. Two corrections, in order: ask the all-in question before quoting so the wife surfaces early, and when a prospect offers to confirm in three hours, take that window rather than pushing it a day for a timezone.
